meta.scene_summary: We are building a more secure, private internet just in time for the AI companies to finish burning it down.

cooking.headline: Amazon is spending $1B to prove that money can indeed silence a server room.
cooking.summary: Amazon is pouring a billion dollars into local infrastructure to smooth over community complaints about their datacenters. It is the corporate equivalent of buying the neighbors noise-canceling headphones because your server fans sound like a jet engine taking off.
cooking.plain_english: Amazon is investing $1 billion into local community projects and infrastructure to address concerns and opposition regarding their datacenter expansion plans.

cooking.headline: Aleph Alpha drops Kolibri, an LLM that actually speaks German without sounding like a tourist.
cooking.summary: Most LLMs handle German like a frantic student using Google Translate, but Aleph Alpha is finally catering to the home crowd. It turns out that teaching a model to respect grammar is a great way to avoid sounding like a broken chatbot.
cooking.plain_english: Aleph Alpha has released a new artificial intelligence model specifically optimized for the German and English languages.

cooking.headline: Zig 0.17.0 is out, proving that some languages prefer stability over moving fast and breaking everything.
cooking.summary: Updating to a new version of Zig feels like moving furniture in your house while the floor is still being built. It is a relief to see a release that focuses on making the language actually usable instead of just adding more syntax sugar.
cooking.plain_english: The Zig programming language has released version 0.17.0, which includes various improvements and updates to the language and its build system.

cooking.headline: Cloudflare is finally letting the peasants into the Enterprise lounge
cooking.summary: Cloudflare is handing out high-tier features to everyone, effectively turning their Enterprise gatekeeping into a public service. It is a bold move to make sure your side project has the same security budget as a Fortune 500 company.
cooking.plain_english: Cloudflare has made several tools previously exclusive to expensive enterprise plans available to all customers at no additional cost.

cooking.headline: Cloudflare's new OHTTP gateway is basically a privacy-focused 'don't look at me' button
cooking.summary: They just launched an OHTTP gateway to help you hide your IP address from the websites you visit. It is the digital equivalent of wearing a trench coat and sunglasses just to go buy a carton of milk.
cooking.plain_english: Cloudflare has introduced a gateway that uses Oblivious HTTP to separate a user's identity from their request, increasing privacy for web browsing.

cooking.headline: Qubes OS 4.3.2 is out for those who find normal security 'too trusting'
cooking.summary: Qubes OS just released an update for people who treat every browser tab like a potential biological hazard. It is the perfect operating system if you want to ensure your computer is more paranoid than you are after three cups of coffee.
cooking.plain_english: Qubes OS, an operating system focused on high security through virtualization, has released version 4.3.2.

cooked.headline: OpenAI's safety team is speedrunning their resignation letters
cooked.summary: It turns out the company building the future of intelligence is having a classic group project meltdown. They are prioritizing speed over safety so aggressively that even the safety team has decided to log off permanently.
cooked.plain_english: Employees from the OpenAI safety team have resigned, citing concerns over the company's internal culture and priorities.

cooked.headline: Google is ending the free trial of their AI utility
cooked.summary: Google decided that giving away free AI models was a great way to acquire users until it was time to actually pay the server bills. It turns out the 'free' era of LLMs has the shelf life of a carton of milk left in the breakroom fridge.
cooked.plain_english: Google is removing free access to its Gemini Flash and Pro artificial intelligence models.

cooked.headline: Palantir's database is now the world's most invasive photo album.
cooked.summary: ICE has been feeding photos of protesters directly into Palantir's software, proving that if there is a data point, someone will eventually try to optimize it for surveillance. It's the ultimate group project where nobody asked for the extra credit, but everyone is getting a failing grade in privacy.
cooked.plain_english: Immigration and Customs Enforcement has been uploading photographs of protesters into a database managed by the data analytics company Palantir.

cooked.headline: A US court just realized that 'deepfake' is a terrible courtroom witness
cooked.summary: A murder conviction was overturned because the prosecution used AI-generated video of the victim to help tell the story. It turns out that bringing a hallucinating witness to the stand is a great way to turn a guilty verdict into a mistrial.
cooked.plain_english: A murder conviction was overturned because the prosecution used an AI-generated video in court, which the judge ruled was inappropriate.
